options.V1: Visibility / purpose flags on the attribute definition

subtallies.name: V1 — a per-attribute visibility / filterability / purpose control on the definition
V2 — does the category decide anything about attributes?
cells: category decides which attributes EXIST (membership, not visibility)
category decides nothing (family / ProductType / attribute set decides)

subtallies.name: V3 — per channel
cells: per-channel at the product level only

rows.h: V2 by product type; per-marketplace selectors
rows.shape: Two flags on every property of the type definition — verified first-party 2026-09-21 (meta-schema page, Purpose: Informational; the record had them only from P2/P3 dumps): hidden — “whether a property should be hidden in Amazon user interfaces”; editable — “whether or not a property value can be modified for an existing item.” Observed editable:true, hidden:false on item_name, variation_theme.name, parentage_level.value; editable:false, hidden:true on child_relationship_type and marketplace_id. Purpose is declared per property group: product_details = “to support search, browse and detail page content”; safety_and_compliance = compliance, hazmat, legal warnings. Filters: the browse-tree guides' Refinements sheet — 2,600,729 rows, 1,407 distinct attributes globally (US 1,035); the search API exposes exactly two refinement axes, brands and classifications. “A new optional attribute is introduced to improve the product detail page.” occurs 267,595 times in release notes. Per-channel = a per-marketplace selector on every value ("selectors": ["marketplace_id","language_tag"]).

rows.h: the richest instance: V1 + V2 + V3 all on the definition
rows.shape: V3 on the definition: MetafieldDefinition.access: MetafieldAccess! {admin, storefront, customerAccount} — live {"admin":"PUBLIC_READ_WRITE","storefront":"PUBLIC_READ","customerAccount":"NONE"} on shopify.color-pattern, storefront: NONE on a custom one; StandardMetafieldDefinitionTemplate.visibleToStorefrontApi: Boolean! (all 28 constrained templates true). V1: capabilities {smartCollectionCondition, adminFilterable, uniqueValues} each {eligible, enabled, status}; pinnedPosition: Int. V2: conditional metafields — “By default, metafield definitions apply to every resource on their owner type … Shoe size is a valid metafield for Shoes but wouldn't apply to Sweaters … Currently, Shopify only supports constraint subtypes that correspond to product categories on Product metafield definitions.” One constraint on shopify.color-pattern pages to 7,750 category ids. Filters: CollectionRuleColumn (15 values) includes PRODUCT_METAFIELD_DEFINITION and VARIANT_METAFIELD_DEFINITION — a definition is itself a first-class filter column at both levels. Live 2026-09-21: membership, not visibility, is what the category decides — Pasta & Noodles has no Flavor at all while Snack Foods has the global one.

rows.h: V3 lives on the product, not the attribute
rows.shape: No field equivalent to Amazon's hidden. Per-channel at product level: excludedDestinations (13-value enum: SHOPPING_ADS · DISPLAY_ADS · LOCAL_INVENTORY_ADS · FREE_LISTINGS · FREE_LOCAL_LISTINGS · YOUTUBE_SHOPPING · … · CLOUD_RETAIL), includedDestinations, shopping_ads_excluded_country, pause; the spec's list of 7 disagrees with the API's 13. Per-surface availability by publication, not flag: [lifestyle_image_link] “only available for browsy surfaces”; [short_title] “only for Demand Gen Ads”. The three requirement markers are the closest thing to a purpose tier: Required (won't serve) · It depends (product/country) · Optional (“boost performance”). custom_label_0-4: ≤1,000 unique values each; buyer visibility not answered. Landing-page match is a stated purpose for variant-identifying values.

rows.h: eleven flags per aspect; V2 by construction
rows.shape: AspectConstraint, exactly 11 properties: aspectEnabledForVariations · aspectMode (“free text or by selecting from available options”) · aspectRequired · itemToAspectCardinality (single/multi, ≤30 values) · aspectUsage (OPTIONAL 136,195 / RECOMMENDED 60,851 — and contradicts aspectRequired by design: required aspects return RECOMMENDED; the two Taxonomy operations disagree on 33 of 421 aspects) · aspectApplicableTo (ITEM 19,206 / PRODUCT 87,560) · aspectDataType (STRING 196,549 / NUMBER 482 / DATE 15 / STRING_ARRAY 0, “reserved for internal use”) · aspectAdvancedDataType (NUMERIC_RANGE, 25) · aspectFormat (int32 229 / double 101 / YYYYMMDD 12 / YYYY 3) · aspectMaxLength (15,629) · expectedRequiredByDate (6) · valueConstraints (429,323 conditional-logic occurrences). relevanceIndicator/searchCount gated to Buyer Demand Data apps (0 in corpus). Buyer filters closed 2026-09-19 on two routes: Seller Center — “Buyers use item specifics to filter their search results”; Browse API Refinement.aspectDistributions, aspect_filter=categoryId:15724,Color:{Red}.

rows.h: a per-slot PURPOSE tier on 100 % of slots; a different vocabulary per feed type
rows.shape: All 383,947 slots carry a comments string, 81 distinct values: @group=Recommended to improve search and browse on Walmart website 258,217 · @group=Required for the item to be visible on Walmart website 58,595 · @group=Recommended to create a variant experience on Walmart website 27,828 (= 6,957 types × the 4 variant fields, the whole tier) · @group=Required to sell on Walmart website 13,781 · @group=Condition Details 6,996. The clearest statement in the thirteen of what an attribute is FOR: sell · be visible · improve search and browse · create a variant experience. The maintenance feed uses a different vocabulary entirely (Product Content to improve search & browse 238,474 · Basic Item Info · Site Experience · Compliance & Regulatory · Images), a fourth on MP_ITEM_MATCH; businessUnit ∈ [SAMSCLUB, WALMART_CA, WALMART_US, ASDA_GM]. Viewing/editing restrictions exist only as workbook column headers (Restrict Viewing by, Restrict Editing For) with no values; searchable/facet/filterable/refinement 0 hits. Display ranking of variant attributes published nowhere. Internal-rule facts sit in the fixed Orderable block.

rows.h: flags on the definition; V2 by construction
rows.shape: attribute_info {input_type (5), input_validation_type (5), format_type (2), date_format_type, attribute_unit_list, max_value_count, is_oem, support_search_value} + mandatory. support_search_value is the only filterability-shaped flag, and no description is quoted. V2: “only last-level categories can retrieve attribute data.” Compliance-as-attribute, dated: a 2026-01-23 announcement adds a blocking validation keyed to attribute_id 101351 against government open data; “Ativação do Atributo de Anvisa como obrigatório”. But tax, size chart, certification, purchase limit, complaint policy are fixed item fields, not attributes. No buyer-visibility flag reported.

rows.h: no visibility flag in either era
rows.shape: Era A: only sort_order on the Annotation group and has_unit/status/is_primary on the axis catalogue; is_variant 0, is_mandatory 0. Era B: id, name, type, is_requried, values[{id,name,icon_url}], value_data_format, is_customizable, requirement_conditions, is_multiple_selection — no filterability, searchability, facet or buyer-visibility flag. V2 + V3 in one sentence: attributes “bound to the specified category, based on your shop's location”; listing_platforms ∈ {TOKOPEDIA, TIKTOK_SHOP} is a per-product channel field. Product-level visibility: is_not_for_sale (GWP-only, hidden from search). Internal rules worked as attributes: EU unit price pairs sku_unit_count with “base unit count” and “unit type” product attributes; Indonesian “Imported Goods” attribute 102254 (values 1000058/1000059, single route). Structured spec 2026-09-21 (api_meta): requirement_conditions[] {condition_type: VALUE_ID_MATCH, attribute_id, attribute_value_id} — “the ‘Battery type’ attribute is required if the seller selects the value ‘Batteries’ for ‘Contains Batteries or Cells?’” — conditional requiredness on the definition; value_data_format (POSITIVE_INT_OR_DECIMAL) applies to cascading attributes only.

rows.h: two visibility enums on the definition (the card's pointer)
rows.shape: CatalogCustomAttributeDefinition.seller_visibility (enum 2) / app_visibility (enum 3): observed SELLER_VISIBILITY_READ_WRITE_VALUES, SELLER_VISIBILITY_HIDDEN, APP_VISIBILITY_READ_WRITE_VALUES; APP_VISIBILITY_READ_ONLY_VALUES rejected live as INVALID_ENUM_VALUE (unreconciled). The cap is expressed in visibility terms: 10 seller-visible + 10 seller-hidden, live-verified. Per object type: ITEM / ITEM_VARIATION visible in Dashboard and API; MODIFIER, MODIFIER_LIST, CATEGORY API-only. Per channel in prose: “The Square Point of Sale application doesn't show custom attributes for any object type.” V2: no — “they appear on every item and item variation in the seller's catalog.” Filterability: no per-custom-attribute flag; searchability only on built-ins (CatalogItemOption.name, sku, abbreviation).

rows.h: V2 is the design: attribute groups attach to categories, with a precedence rule
rows.shape: “An attribute group is a grouping of attribute assignments that's attached to a category. Attributes can belong to more than one attribute group. The attribute assignments display on the product details page and during some product comparisons.” Three layers: global (system object type Product) → the classification category's groups and its ancestors' → the browse category's (Category.getProductAttributeModel()). Override precedence: category group overrides global with the same ID; sub-category overrides parent (single-route). Entry point: Product.getAttributeModel(). V1: only @system: xsd:boolean; no shown/hidden flag. V3: the classification-vs-primary split (attributes vs breadcrumbs). Currency warning: OCAPI deprecated April 2026; the whole help.salesforce.com corpus unreproducible.

rows.h: V3 is first-class as requiredness; V1 carries the filter flag
rows.shape: Per channel is a table: pim_catalog_attribute_requirement.required under UNIQUE (channel_id, family_id, attribute_id); on the wire "attribute_requirements":{"ecommerce":[…],"mobile":[…],"print":[…]} — models “required on the web but not at the till” exactly. scopable is the per-channel flag on the definition (immutable; a scopable attribute cannot be an axis, AXES_WRONG_TYPE); every value is {locale, scope, data}. V1: useable_as_grid_filter (true on auto_exposure, color; no vendor definition quoted), sort_order, group → AttributeGroup, unique, localizable, is_locale_specific. V2 absent (0 hits, controls 203/62/117) — but a separate pim_catalog_category_attribute attaches attributes to the category record. Headline purpose is completeness: “which family attributes are required for the completeness calculation.” No visible flag anywhere.

rows.h: per (product, attribute); filterability decided by global-vs-local
rows.shape: WC_Product_Attribute.visible → is_visible 1/0 in the product's _product_attributes blob (meaning not stated in the record). On the definition: attribute_public int(1) DEFAULT 1 → REST has_archives — DDL default 1, lands as 0 through REST; all four live rows read 0. Filterability structural: wc_product_attributes_lookup re-normalises the variation's slug to a term id for global attributes only; local ones skipped (// Custom product attribute, not suitable for attribute-based filtering.), gated by woocommerce_attribute_lookup_enabled. Ordering is a purpose: attribute_orderby ∈ menu_order|name|name_num|id — “affects the sorting order of the dropdown selector(s)”. V2 absent (500 product_cat lines, 0 touch an attribute taxonomy). V3 not answered.

rows.h: one flag, plus a deprecation caveat on the whole level mechanism
rows.shape: AttributeDefinition {isSearchable, inputHint (SingleLine|MultiLine), inputTip?, label, isRequired, attributeConstraint, level}; no meaning stated for inputHint/inputTip. AttributeLevelEnum [Product, Variant] — “Product: Attribute is defined at Product level (not supported by Product Projection Search)”, and Product Projection Search is deprecated; nested/set types do not support isSearchable. Shown vs internal: not answered; nearest is per request — “Variant-level Attribute names to include … Product-level Attributes are silently omitted.” on a PDP read model. V2 absent: api/types/category/ has no attributes/productType property (adjacent unmeasured: Category.custom?: CustomFields). level is immutable in the UI.

rows.h: maximum resolution: one flag per use; V3 as value scope
rows.shape: catalog_eav_attribute, 24 columns merged: is_global, is_visible, is_searchable, is_filterable, is_comparable, is_visible_on_front, is_html_allowed_on_front, is_used_for_price_rules, is_filterable_in_search, used_in_product_listing, used_for_sort_by, apply_to, is_visible_in_advanced_search, position, is_wysiwyg_enabled, is_used_for_promo_rules, is_required_in_admin_store, is_used_in_grid, is_visible_in_grid, is_filterable_in_grid, frontend_input_renderer + search_weight float NOT NULL default 1 (CatalogSearch) + additional_data text (Swatches). Closed at source 2026-09-19: defaults is_global/is_visible = 1, all others 0; is_filterable is a three-valued enum — 0 No · 1 Filterable (with results) · 2 Filterable (no results) — “Can be used only with catalog input type Yes/No, Dropdown, Multiple Select and Price.” V3 = value scope: SCOPE_STORE=0, SCOPE_GLOBAL=1, SCOPE_WEBSITE=2; values UNIQUE (entity_id, attribute_id, store_id), option labels per store view. Internal rules as flags: is_used_for_promo_rules, is_used_for_price_rules (written by no PropertyMapper). V2 absent over 352 <table> blocks; the attribute set gates data entry.

coupling: A0↔A5: commercetools (level beside isSearchable) and Shopify (ownerType beside access/capabilities) carry level and visibility as independent fields on one definition; no record ties them — “family-level = visible” has no precedent.
